name: Agent-First Terminal
synopsis: Let your AI agent work in a real terminal you can watch — and take the keyboard back whenever you want, from your phone if you are not at the machine.
intent: Expose Rust APIs for opening, tracking, resizing, signaling, and streaming one or many trusted local terminal sessions
Coordinate multiple human and automated input actors with shared or exclusive TTL leases and immediate human preemption
Take secret input in a session without publishing anything derived from its bytes, suspending every non-human actor until the person ends the window
Expose the same multi-session runtime through a loopback-only bearer-protected OpenAPI 3.2 HTTP API for external controllers
Let the afterminal CLI open a trusted local DOM-rendered terminal window over a new runtime or attach midway to sessions owned by an already-running API server
Keep the PTY runtime independent of any UI host or application-specific task model, with AFUI hosting only the CLI's window
Provide bounded scrollback subscriptions without coupling terminal output to any UI data model
mutations: Answer the cursor-position and status queries a program makes of its terminal (ESC[6n and ESC[5n), reporting the cursor as the screen stands; without this ConPTY emits nothing at all and a Windows session never starts, while the private ESC[?6n form is deliberately left unanswered rather than answered wrongly
Resolve the default session program per platform: COMSPEC on Windows rather than /bin/sh, and never SHELL there, whose one common value is an MSYS path CreateProcessW cannot resolve
Run the runtime suites and the API, window and delivery smokes on Windows in continuous integration, so the platform is exercised on every push instead of for the first time during a release

bonds.reason: CLI discovery, output routing, redaction, and protocol events follow Agent-First Data conventions
The `api` feature builds the afterminal CLI window on Agent-First UI, which owns the browser process, its disposable profile, the UI credential, and the security headers
